title: DoorDash Starts Delivering Toilet Paper and Other Groceries
summary: DoorDash, the largest food delivery app in the U.S., is expanding its services to include deliveries from convenience stores like 7-Eleven and Wawa. This accelerated rollout, prompted by the coronavirus pandemic, allows customers to order essential goods such as toilet paper and other packaged items. The company currently has over 1,800 convenience stores listed on its app across the U.S.

title: Home Depot Halts Sales of N95 Masks Amid Shortage, Company Says (Published 2020)
summary: Home Depot has halted sales of N95 masks at all of its North American stores and redirected them to healthcare providers and emergency responders due to the coronavirus pandemic. Other retailers like Lowe's and Target have also taken similar actions, while 3M, a mask manufacturer, has expressed concern over retailers continuing to sell protective gear. The move aims to address the critical shortage of personal protective equipment for frontline workers.

title: Jessica Alba's The Honest Company Has Donated 3 Million Diapers To Help Families In Need
summary: Jessica Alba's The Honest Company has donated three million diapers, 20,000 wipes, and 20,000 personal care products to families in need during the coronavirus pandemic. Alba emphasized that these donations address the critical needs of families facing difficult choices between essentials like diapers and food. Her husband, Cash Warren, also contributed through his company, Pair of Thieves, by donating profits to purchase relief supplies and masks for front-line workers.

title: EBay pledges $100M to help small businesses move online
summary: eBay has launched its "Up & Running" accelerator program, investing $100 million to help North American small businesses without an online presence transition to e-commerce. The program offers free basic eBay stores for three months, waived selling fees for up to 500 items, and provides marketing tools, discounted shipping, and educational resources. This initiative responds to the increased focus on e-commerce due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with 70% of small businesses reportedly lacking an online presence before the outbreak.

title: Infographic: Retailers’ cage-free egg pledges
summary: U.S. egg producers are converting to cage-free systems as North American retailers commit to sourcing only cage-free eggs. While some retailers already exclusively sell cage-free eggs, many others, including major grocery chains, are still in transition, with most aiming for completion by 2025 or 2026. This shift is also driven by new laws in several U.S. states requiring cage-free egg production and sales.

title: Uber Aids Idled Rideshare Drivers With Job Listings
summary: Uber is launching "Work Hub," an initiative to connect its rideshare drivers, who are experiencing diminished income due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with alternative job listings. These opportunities include roles within Uber, such as Uber Freight or Uber Eats, and with other companies like Domino’s, Shipt, and CareGuide, covering positions in food production, warehousing, and customer service. The company also encouraged drivers to join Uber Eats, which has seen increased demand, and is contributing to a Restaurant Employee Relief Fund.

title: SoFi acquires banking tech firm Galileo for $1.2 billion
summary: SoFi announced its acquisition of Galileo, a banking tech firm that powers companies like Robinhood and Chime, for $1.2 billion. The deal involves $875 million in SoFi shares, $75 million in cash, and $250 million in debt financing. SoFi plans to operate Galileo as an independent entity, providing white-label technology services globally, despite both companies recently experiencing turbulence.

title: BlackBerry uncovers hacker tools that it says opened data servers for a decade
summary: BlackBerry has released a report detailing how five separate groups linked to the Chinese government have been targeting Linux systems for a decade. These hackers have used novel techniques, including disguising malicious tools as advertising software, to exfiltrate vast amounts of data from servers. The report highlights a significant blind spot in cybersecurity, as Linux powers critical global infrastructure like stock exchanges and major cloud services.

title: Piper Sandler Completes 39th Semi-Annual Generation Z Survey of 5,200 U.S. Teens
summary: Piper Sandler completed its 39th semi-annual "Taking Stock With Teens" survey, revealing a 13% year-over-year decrease in self-reported teen spending to $2,300, the lowest since fall 2011, largely influenced by the COVID-19 pandemic. The survey of 5,200 U.S. teens highlighted food as the top spending priority and environmental concerns as the primary social/political issue, with "Coronavirus" ranking second. Key trends include Amazon's dominance in e-commerce, a significant drop in female cosmetic spending, and the continued popularity of Nike and lululemon in fashion, alongside TikTok's debut as a major social media platform.

title: Simply Good Foods builds inventories as Covid-19 boosts e-commerce sales
summary: Simply Good Foods Co. is increasing its inventory levels and reallocating marketing spend in response to altered consumer purchasing behavior caused by Covid-19, which has significantly boosted e-commerce sales. The company is moving from five-to-six weeks of stock to eight-to-ten weeks for its top SKUs to ensure safety stock and meet increased online demand for brands like Quest Nutrition and Atkins Nutritionals. This shift is expected to have a short-term impact of US$10-15m on cash flow, but the company remains confident in its supply chain.

title: SPXL vs. UPRO: Head-To-Head ETF Comparison
summary: This article provides a head-to-head comparison of two leveraged S&P 500 ETFs, SPXL and UPRO, detailing their fees, performance, holdings, and ESG scores. It offers a comprehensive overview for investors to make informed decisions by comparing various metrics from expense ratios and AUM to technical indicators and analyst takes. Both ETFs offer 3x daily long leverage to the S&P 500 Index, making them tools for investors with a bullish short-term outlook on U.S. large cap stocks.

title: Amazon stops accepting new online grocery customers amid surging demand
summary: Amazon is implementing new measures to manage surging online grocery demand, including placing new customers on a waitlist and shortening Whole Foods' public hours to prioritize online orders. The company is actively increasing capacity by hiring additional workers and transitioning a new store into an online order warehouse. Despite these efforts, Amazon acknowledges that high demand and social distancing may continue to make delivery windows challenging for customers.

title: Amazon Revenue by Year, Worldwide (In US$ Millions)
summary: This article provides a historical overview of Amazon's worldwide annual revenue from 1996 to 2019, highlighting its growth trajectory. It notes Amazon's achievement of reaching $100 billion in annual sales in just 21 years and its record revenue of $280,522 million in 2019. The article also includes a brief company profile of Amazon.com, Inc.

title: Amazon Costs and Expenses by Year
summary: The article analyzes Amazon's costs and expenses by year, showing total operating expenses increased 20.6% YoY in 2019 to $265,981 million. It highlights significant increases in marketing and sales expenses, technology and content costs, cost of sales, and fulfillment costs during the same period. The article also provides a brief overview of Amazon.com, Inc.'s history and key products.

title: Amazon Total Operating Expenses by Year
summary: Amazon's total operating expenses reached an all-time high of $265,981 million in 2019, representing a 20.6% year-over-year increase and 94.8% of its overall revenue. The article details Amazon's historical operating expenditures from 1996 through 2019, highlighting significant growth and milestones. It also provides background on Amazon.com, Inc., its founding, key products, and market value.

title: Amazon Total Operating Expenses by Quarter
summary: This article details Amazon's total operating expenses by quarter from Q1 1997 to Q4 2019, highlighting key growth periods and record highs. It notes that Amazon's operating expenses reached a record $83,558 million in Q4 2019, representing 95.6% of its total revenue, and provides context on the company's financial growth and history.

title: Pfizer’s digital chief: Technology can speed the race to a COVID-19 vaccine
summary: Lidia Fonseca, Pfizer's Chief Digital and Technology Officer, is leveraging technology to support the company's race for a COVID-19 vaccine, enabling remote work for thousands of employees and facilitating data sharing and collaboration with other biopharmaceutical companies. Her team built a "scientific cloud" on Amazon Web Services to centralize Pfizer's previously siloed data, dramatically increasing its value for research. Fonseca emphasizes technology's role in empowering scientists with information to make informed decisions and accelerate the development of life-changing breakthroughs.

title: 2019 Letter to Shareholders
summary: Jeff Bezos's 2019 Letter to Shareholders details Amazon's response to the COVID-19 crisis, highlighting efforts to support customers and employees, including safety measures, wage increases, job creation, and combating price gouging. The letter also covers Amazon's broader initiatives beyond COVID-19, such as The Climate Pledge for carbon neutrality and significant investments in job creation, employee training, and community programs. It contrasts the 2019 situation with Amazon's founding principles from the 1997 shareholder letter, emphasizing long-term focus and customer obsession.

title: Watch FAT Brands CEO on How The Coronavirus Impacted Business
summary: FAT Brands CEO, Andy Wiederhorn, discusses the varied impact of the coronavirus pandemic on his company's 400 franchised restaurants across eight different brands. He highlights the shift to delivery for burger and chicken restaurants, while casual dining and steak houses experienced significant declines. Wiederhorn also addresses concerns about food supply chains, the need for government support for small businesses, and anticipated changes in consumer behavior and restaurant operations post-pandemic.

title: Exclusive: Amazon deploys thermal cameras at warehouses to scan for fevers faster
summary: Amazon.com Inc has begun using thermal cameras at its warehouses to more quickly screen workers for fevers, a key symptom of the coronavirus. This represents an effort to maintain operations and contain the virus' spread without fully closing warehouses, a move that comes amid reports of infections at over 50 U.S. facilities and calls from unions to close buildings. The camera systems, which are faster and require less contact than forehead thermometers, are being deployed in warehouses near Los Angeles and Seattle, and at Whole Foods stores.

title: Large Cap Tech Stocks Continue to Throw Their Weight Around
summary: Large-cap tech stocks, particularly those in the Nasdaq 100, are demonstrating resilience and leading recovery efforts in capital markets amidst the coronavirus pandemic. Companies like Amazon and Microsoft are driving this trend, with the Nasdaq 100 showing a 1% year-to-date gain compared to the S&P 500's 11% decline. Investors can gain exposure through ETFs like FTEC, XLK, and RWLS, which offers a large-cap over small-cap strategy.

title: Wayfair Appoints Jim Miller as Chief Technology Officer
summary: Wayfair Inc. has appointed Jim Miller as its permanent Chief Technology Officer, a role he had held on an interim basis since August 2019. Miller, with extensive experience from Google, Cisco, and Amazon, will lead Wayfair's global tech operations and engineering team. He will also step down from Wayfair's board, a position he held for four years.

title: Geared Consumer Discretionary ETFs For An Altered Retail Landscape
summary: This article discusses how the COVID-19 pandemic significantly altered the retail landscape, impacting traditional retailers while boosting e-commerce giants like Amazon. It examines two leveraged ETFs, Direxion Daily Consumer Discretionary Bull 3X Shares (WANT) and Direxion Daily Consumer Discretionary Bear 3X Shares (PASS), as ways for active traders to play these trends. The article highlights that while consumer discretionary spending is projected to decline, WANT still offers appeal due to its significant Amazon exposure, while PASS benefits from the broader retail downturn.

title: Metlife buys giant Amazon fulfillment center in Shakopee
summary: Metlife has purchased an 860,000-square-foot Amazon fulfillment center in Shakopee, Minnesota, for $118 million. This distribution center was Amazon's initial major investment in the southwest metro area. The sale reflects significant activity in the commercial real estate market, with related articles discussing other large property deals.

title: Spotting A Winner Among Internet ETFs
summary: The article highlights the Global Internet Giants ETF (OGIG) as a strong performer among Internet ETFs, particularly due to the "staying in" theme accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. OGIG, with major holdings like Amazon, Alibaba, and Tencent, focuses on internet and e-commerce sectors with quality and growth potential. The fund benefits from the rapid shift to online retail and work-from-home trends, suggesting significant long-term growth potential.

title: Coronavirus pandemic and online media consumption: settling into the New Normal
summary: This article discusses how online media consumption in Europe has begun to level off after an initial surge during the early stages of the coronavirus pandemic lockdown. It highlights that the "new normal" has settled in, with some categories that saw initial growth, such as General News, Instant Messaging, Food/Groceries Retail, and Entertainment, now showing signs of fatigue as activity stabilizes. The piece also includes a timeline of key pandemic events in Europe leading up to the lockdowns.

title: IZEA Announces Twitch Influencer Marketing Workflow Support in IZEAx Unity Suite
summary: IZEA Worldwide, Inc. has launched beta support for Twitch influencer marketing workflows within its IZEAx Unity Suite, allowing marketers to integrate Twitch live stream sponsorships into their campaigns. This new feature enables standalone Twitch sponsorships or their inclusion in broader multi-channel initiatives, leveraging the platform's increased viewership due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The workflow was developed in collaboration with a Fortune 500 company and aims to connect brands with Twitch's captive audience, who show a higher propensity to purchase non-essential products.

title: Ford’s Lincoln And Rivian Cancel Electric SUV Plans, Citing COVID-19 Impact
summary: Lincoln, Ford's luxury brand, has canceled an electric SUV it planned to develop with startup partner Rivian, citing the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Although other collaborations between Ford and Rivian will continue, this specific project was halted due to difficulties exacerbated by the pandemic, including remote work challenges and delayed vehicle production. This decision comes as Ford invests heavily in electrification, but the future demand for electric vehicles remains uncertain given the collapse of the oil market and changes in regulatory incentives.

title: Build-A-Bear introduces online activity program
summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop launched "Workshop Wednesdays," an online program providing creative activities and entertainment for families during the COVID-19 pandemic. The initiative includes new weekly activities, enhanced online Bear Builder features, and access to Build-A-Bear Radio and YouTube content. This move aims to maintain engagement with its core audience while physical stores are closed, as the toy industry faces challenges and Build-A-Bear itself furloughed staff due to the pandemic's impact.
